text: 🇲🇽⚓ "Sovereignty is not inherited once and for all. It is defended, exercised and built every day." "Once Spain recognized our independence, Mexican soil became the desire of other empires of the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 201st anniversary of the Consolidation of Independence at Sea, Mexico City, Nov 23, 2026 On November 23, 1825, the last Spanish troops left the fortress of San Juan de Ulúa in Veracruz, four years after independence, following a naval blockade organized by frigate captain Pedro Sainz de Baranda. At the ceremony marking 201 years, Sheinbaum went through what came after: Spain's failed reconquest attempt in 1829, stopped in Tampico; the Pastry War with France in 1838–39; the US invasion of 1846–48, "which took more than half of the national territory"; the second French intervention, defeated in 1867 under Benito Juárez; and in the 20th century, the 1913 coup against Madero and the attempted US invasion of 1914.

🚨🇲🇽 "Just as we sent 94 criminals to the United States, we ask for reciprocity." "There are pending issues, several, many, that we have been requesting from the United States." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 TV host Inés Gómez Mont had an Interpol red notice over Mexico's complaints and arrest warrants against her; Sheinbaum said "there is all the evidence" she dealt in fake invoices. The red notice was withdrawn about a month ago, and she was detained in the US for immigration reasons and is being deported to Spain, since she also holds Spanish nationality. Mexico will file a complaint with Interpol over why the notice was withdrawn and send a diplomatic note to the US, "because they know there is an arrest warrant." Mexico has already requested her extradition from Spain. Among the pending requests: the Ayotzinapa cases, including the Iguala "juez de barandilla," whose file she handed personally to Marco Rubio, and who has still not been extradited or deported.

🇲🇽⚓ "Independence was not a gift or a concession. It was a conquest by those who dared to fight for a free nation." "Today, as two centuries ago, we have the determination to keep building our own path with dignity, with independence, with justice, and with the conviction that Mexico's destiny is decided only by the people of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 201st anniversary of the Consolidation of Independence at Sea, Mexico City, Nov 23, 2026 Sheinbaum honored the Navy, from the first naval squadron that blockaded San Juan de Ulúa in 1825 to today's force: Mexican-developed unmanned aircraft for surveillance, secure radio and communication systems, oceanographic and weather buoys in the Pacific to improve hurricane forecasts and early warning, sargassum cleanup in the Caribbean, and the modernization of ports.

🇲🇽☕ "Nestlé has to pay what it has to pay for the coffee, for the kilo of coffee." "It can't be that the market sets the price of coffee for the coffee growers, even through intermediaries (...) The coffee growers are right and we are going to support them." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 25, 2026 Coffee growers in Tapachula, Chiapas, protested against the multinational. According to the question, they are being paid 43 pesos, and 165,000 families depend on the crop. Sheinbaum said coffee is sold at 580 pesos and bought at 43, and the growers are asking for 50 to 60 pesos. She said that since yesterday she has instructed Agriculture Secretary Columba López to back the growers in their negotiation with the company and to go to Chiapas. "Nestlé has to pay, and it has to buy directly from the producers."
